chunks: And from him, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurarah ibn A'yan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

If a man is prevented (from completing his Hajj), he should send his offering (hady). If he recovers and finds lightness in himself, let him proceed if he thinks he will reach his offering before it is slaughtered. If he arrives in Mecca before his offering is slaughtered, let him remain in his state of Ihram until he performs the rituals and slaughters his offering, and there is nothing upon him. If he arrives in Mecca and his offering has already been slaughtered, then upon him is the Hajj of next year and the Umrah.
I said: And if he dies before reaching Mecca? He said: If it is his Farewell Hajj (Hajjat al-Islam), they perform Hajj and Umrah on his behalf; for it is merely a debt upon him.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: State of consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.هَدْي: Sacrificial animal offered by the pilgrim

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for a pilgrim who is prevented from completing Hajj or dies before reaching Mecca?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elaborates on the fiqh of the *muhsar* (one prevented from completing Hajj), distinguishing between cases where the pilgrim returns home versus those who remain in Mecca to complete rituals. It provides precise legal criteria for the timing of the sacrificial animal's slaughter relative to the pilgrim's arrival, reflecting the Imami school's detailed approach to ritual obligations. The ruling also extends to the case of death, ensuring that the obligation of Hajj al-Islam is fulfilled by a proxy if it was the pilgrim's first obligatory Hajj.
